findings.mechanism: Section::append stores a strong Rc to the parent in child.parent while the parent holds the child in its children Vec. Every parent/child pair is a reference cycle, so when parser::parse's Parsed.root (Rc) is dropped at the end of Service::handle the refcounts never reach zero and the whole section tree (titles, nodes, vectors) is never freed. Rust has no cycle collector.
findings.cause: strong Rc back-link for breadcrumbs; should be Weak<Section> (upgrade in parent()). Also hits the error path: a document that fails with EmptyTitle after some headings drops a partially built tree that is also cyclic.
findings.evidence: Built release and ran --iterations 1000/5000/20000: peak RSS 13 MB / 34 MB / 130 MB, i.e. linear, about 6 KB per document, with no live data retained by Service (it only holds two counters). Code review: Service::handle drops `parsed` and `listing` on return, nothing else references the tree.

findings.mechanism: Service holds only the handled/rejected u64 counters; no per-request collection.
findings.evidence: Read the code; the struct has no collections and the growth measured is explained by the Section cycle.
findings.discriminator: Service state is two integers and does not grow in size; main's accumulators are scalars too.

findings.mechanism: toc::render clones children Vec<Rc> and breadcrumb Strings per call, which are temporaries.
findings.evidence: Read the code: the clones and the output String are dropped when the call returns; they only bump refcounts transiently and are balanced.
findings.discriminator: Temporary Rc clones are released at scope end, so refcounts return to the pre-call values; the only unbalanced count is the parent link in section.rs.
